records.summary: States a community poll is required before introducing road safety measures on local streets.
records.source_quote: A community poll is required before introducing any road safety measures onto local streets.

records.summary: Designated November as Road Safety Month in Beaches-East York and launched an online tool to collect community poll support for road safety measures during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: We're making November #RoadSafetyMonth in Beaches-East York! ... so I've created an online tool to collect support and ensure our efforts to make streets safer don't fall behind.

records.summary: States environmental considerations such as permeable paving and tree protection must come first in front yard parking pad rules.
records.source_quote: nothing has changed in terms of the requirements to have permeable paving and to protect trees. The environmental considerations have to come first and foremost.

records.summary: Supports enabling EV ownership as a significant part of meeting Toronto's climate goals.
records.source_quote: We have a long way to go to meet our climate goals - enabling EV ownership will play a significant part.

records.summary: Supports opening up front yard parking pad application process to make more households eligible, framed as incentivizing EV ownership.
records.source_quote: This is a big step forward to incentivizing electric vehicle ownership to meet our climate goals.

records.summary: Council lifted the parking pad ban north of the Danforth and made changes to open up the application process for front yard parking.
records.source_quote: We’re inching forward on parking pads with good progress at Council yesterday! The ban north of the Danforth has been lifted and we’ve made a number of changes towards opening up the application process to make more households eligible for front yard parking.

records.summary: New EV charging stations installed in the neighbourhood — one at Bowmore/Eastwood, another opening on Westlake.
records.source_quote: we have some new EV chargers in the neighbourhood! One station is at Bowmore/Eastwood with another opening on Westlake next weekend.

records.summary: Brought forward a road map of recommendations to Council to boost small business, keep main streets thriving, and support local shops; Council unanimously approved it.
records.source_quote: Yesterday, Council unanimously approved my road map to boost small business, keep main streets thriving and support our mom and pops.

records.summary: States that the Toronto Office of Rebuild & Recovery report had 83 recommendations for a healthy physical, social, and economic recovery.
records.source_quote: The Toronto Office of Rebuild & Recovery report had 83 recommendations for a healthy physical, social, and economic recovery.

records.summary: States Toronto needs a new fiscal deal with senior levels of government, citing the TORR report.
records.source_quote: The TORR report lays clear the need for a new deal for Toronto.

records.summary: States municipal government most directly affects residents' day-to-day lives and resources/funding from government partners should reflect that.
records.source_quote: This is the level of government that most directly affects folks day-to-day lives. We need the resources and funding from our government partners to reflect this reality.

records.summary: States that high commissions (as much as 35%) charged by food delivery apps hurt local restaurants and Toronto should address this as LA, New York, and Seattle have.
records.source_quote: Some popular meal service apps charge restaurants commissions as high as 35%. With local businesses hurting so badly right now, we should be tackling this like LA, New York and Seattle have.

records.summary: Observes that restaurants, cafes, and bars have been struggling during the pandemic and that delivery app fees worsen their margins.
records.source_quote: Restaurants, cafes, and bars have been having a tough time throughout the pandemic... However, many of these apps have significant fees that restaurants must pay. This hurts their bottom line and makes the margins even more thin.

records.summary: States road safety is his top local priority.
records.source_quote: Road safety is my top local priority and throughout the pandemic I've been working with residents to introduce new traffic calming measures throughout the neighbourhood.

records.summary: Notes City by-laws require a polling process to introduce traffic calming measures on residential streets, and that COVID-19 has caused large backlogs.
records.source_quote: City by-laws require a polling process in order to introduce these measures on residential streets. With large backlogs due to the COVID-19 pandemic

records.summary: Working directly with community to run polls on road safety interventions to bypass City backlog and advance traffic calming measures.
records.source_quote: I'm working directly with the community to run polls on road safety interventions so that our efforts to make our streets safer don't fall behind.

records.summary: Posted a digital list of community polls on his website (bradbradford.ca/petitions) for residents to show support for traffic calming on their streets.
records.source_quote: On my website is a digital list of community polls which can be used to show support. Check out bradbradford.ca/petitions (link in bio) for more information and a list of active polls.

records.quote_text: Road safety is my top local priority.
records.speaker: Brad Bradford

records.summary: Started an online petition to rename a laneway south of Gerrard and east of Wayland after Reese Fallon, a victim of the 2018 Danforth shooting.
records.source_quote: Neighbour support is needed to officially rename a laneway in Toronto. I started an online petition to gather this support. Please visit my website at bradbradford.ca/reeselane (link in bio) for more information or to sign the petition.

records.summary: Supports naming a laneway after Reese Fallon, a victim of the 2018 Danforth shooting, at a location south of Gerrard and east of Wayland.
records.source_quote: We want to honour her short but impactful time with us by naming a laneway after her. The proposed location is south of Gerrard and east of Wayland. This location was chosen because of the proximity to her home, her schools, and her friends.

records.summary: States that procuring new subways, streetcars, and buses is as important as transit expansion for meeting service goals.
records.source_quote: Procuring these additional subways, streetcars, and buses are just as important as transit expansion in terms of meeting our service goals.

records.summary: States Toronto is contributing its fair share and calls on Provincial and Federal governments to match contributions for transit investment.
records.source_quote: The City is contributing our fair share to these investments. Toronto is the economic engine of Canada and we need the Provincial and Federal governments to step up, match our contributions, and build a 21st century system with us.

records.summary: Organized/participated in the Beach Pick-Me-Up community cleanup event with Tiffany Pratt at Woodbine Beach.
records.source_quote: we're throwing it back to the Beach Pick-Me-Up with @thetiffanypratt! It was an incredible turnout from the community and the commitment to keeping our shared spaces beautiful was fantastic.

records.event_label: Beach Pick-Me-Up
records.source_quote: we're throwing it back to the Beach Pick-Me-Up with @thetiffanypratt!

records.summary: States that restaurants and bars need innovative support during indoor dining shutdown.
records.source_quote: Running a restaurant or bar is tough at the best of times. Now with indoor dining shut down, we need to take innovative steps to support small businesses.

records.summary: Describes the CafeTO patio program as a success.
records.source_quote: The #CafeTO patios have been a huge success

records.pledge_text: Looking at extending CafeTO patios through the winter and into next spring and summer.
records.specifics: Extension of CafeTO patios through winter, spring, and summer
records.source_quote: we're looking at how we can extend them through the winter, into next spring and summer

records.event_label: Fairmount Park Bake Oven makeover
records.source_quote: The Fairmount Park Bake Oven got a makeover, courtesy of the community! Thanks to Barry Ross, Dieter Epp, John Corcoran, Scott Rogers, and Joseph Romain for putting their own time and resources in to make this community even more special!

records.summary: Canvassed for neighbour support to name a laneway in memory of Reese Fallon, a victim of the 2018 Danforth Shooting.
records.source_quote: Emotional afternoon canvassing for neighbour support to name a laneway in memory of Reese Fallon, one of the two victims whose life was tragically cut short in the Danforth Shooting on July 22, 2018.

records.pledge_text: Together with Reese Fallon's family, will work to name a laneway after her near her home, schools, and friends.
records.specifics: Proposed laneway location close to her home and the schools she attended; supporters can sign on at bradbradford.ca/reeselane
records.source_quote: With her family, we would like to name a Laneway after her. This would be a legacy to her short yet impactful time among us. The proposed location is close to her home, the schools that she attended and to the many friends who cherished her.

records.summary: States the hospitality industry has been uniquely and devastatingly impacted by the pandemic and relies heavily on face-to-face interactions.
records.source_quote: The unique and devastating impact on the hospitality industry throughout the pandemic does not need to be re-stated. It's a tough business that relies heavily on face-to-face interactions to stay profitable.

records.summary: States small businesses and the hospitality sector are a strength of Toronto.
records.source_quote: Our incredible small businesses and hospitality sector are a strength of Toronto, and we're looking forward to growing back even stronger.

records.summary: Served as Small Business lead on Mayor John Tory's Economic Support and Recovery Task Force, consulting weekly with business owners and advocating to provincial and federal partners.
records.source_quote: As the Small Business lead for Mayor @johntory's Economic Support and Recovery Task Force, I spoke with hundreds of business owners each week. This feedback and open dialogue shaped my advocacy to our provincial and federal partners and allowed for programs that would better support our small businesses.

records.summary: States that mopeds, electric scooters, and motorcycles must stay on the road, not in the cycle track, and only pedal-assisted e-bikes are permitted in the cycle track.
records.source_quote: Remember that e-bikes are only allowed if they are pedal assisted! Mopeds, electric scooters, and motorcycles need to stay on the road for everyone's safety.

records.summary: Joined 55 Division on Danforth and Woodbine during evening commute to educate cyclists on rules for the new cycle track.
records.source_quote: Out on Danforth and Woodbine for the evening commute with @55_division last night educating folks on what is and isn't allowed in the new cycle track.

records.event_label: Cycle track education ride-along with 55 Division
records.source_quote: Out on Danforth and Woodbine for the evening commute with @55_division last night educating folks on what is and isn't allowed in the new cycle track.

records.summary: States that procuring new TTC vehicles will ensure Toronto is prepared for transit demand in a post-pandemic world.
records.source_quote: Procuring new #TTC vehicles will ensure that we're prepared for demand in a post-pandemic world.

records.summary: States Toronto is the economic lifeblood of Canada and needs support from provincial and federal partners to reflect that.
records.source_quote: Toronto is the economic lifeblood of this country and we need support from our Provincial and Federal partners to reflect that.

records.summary: States the TTC will be crucial to Toronto's pandemic recovery and that planning for post-pandemic transit needs must begin now.
records.source_quote: Our transit network will be crucial to our recovery and we know that we need to start planning now for our post-pandemic needs.

records.summary: States that other levels of government should join the City in funding TTC vehicle acquisition.
records.source_quote: This is a significant investment from the City and we're looking for the other levels of government to join us.

records.summary: Joined Mayor John Tory to announce City investment in acquiring more TTC vehicles, including 80 subway trains, 13 streetcars, 300 hybrid buses, 300 e-buses, and 70 Wheel-Trans buses.
records.source_quote: I joined Mayor @johntory this morning to announce a significant investment into acquiring more #TTC vehicles to meet rising demand.

records.event_label: TTC vehicle investment announcement with Mayor John Tory
records.source_quote: I joined Mayor @johntory this morning to announce a significant investment into acquiring more #TTC vehicles to meet rising demand.

records.quote_text: Keeping the #TTC moving will help to ensure that the economic engine of Canada is running smoothly.
records.speaker: Brad Bradford

records.summary: Encourages safe travel on the new Danforth complete street when heading to work or supporting local businesses.
records.source_quote: When you're heading out to work or to support local businesses on #DestinationDanforth, travel safely! Check out these quick tips to protect yourself and others on the new complete street.

records.summary: States the city needs smart, practical solutions to support the transition to electric vehicles in neighbourhoods.
records.source_quote: We need smart, practical solutions to support the transition towards electric vehicles in our neighbourhoods.

records.summary: Supports modernizing local infrastructure ('bringing our infrastructure into the 21st century').
records.source_quote: bringing our infrastructure into the 21st century!

records.event_label: Meeting with neighbours on Fernwood Park Avenue
records.topic_focus: road safety, EV transition, and infrastructure
records.source_quote: Great meeting with neighbours on Fernwood Park Avenue to discuss road safety and bringing our infrastructure into the 21st century!

records.summary: States that residents need to be able to use local beaches safely.
records.source_quote: Our community is home to some of the most beautiful beaches in Canada and we need to ensure that folks are able to use them safely.

records.summary: Met with City staff to discuss steps to improve safety on the waterfront.
records.source_quote: I met with staff last week to determine what steps we can take to improve safety on the waterfront!

records.event_label: Visit to Woodbine Beach
records.source_quote: Our community is home to some of the most beautiful beaches in Canada

records.summary: States commitment to ongoing work to address systemic racism and create a more equal society.
records.source_quote: We know that there is much more work to be done to truly make our society equal, but we are fully committed to that work.

records.summary: Hosted a virtual community meeting covering topics including community safety during the pandemic and systemic racism.
records.source_quote: Thank you to everyone from the community who joined our virtual community meeting last night! ... We covered a wide variety of topics, from general community safety during the pandemic to addressing systemic racism.

records.event_label: Virtual Community Meeting
records.topic_focus: community safety during the pandemic and systemic racism
records.source_quote: Thank you to everyone from the community who joined our virtual community meeting last night!

records.summary: States surface transit has played an important role during the pandemic, moving essential workers across the city.
records.source_quote: Surface transit has played an incredibly important role throughout the pandemic. Our buses and streetcars have moved thousands of essential workers across the city every day, keeping it functioning over the past several months.

records.summary: Supports priority bus routes, stating they will produce more frequent service, less crowding, and more efficient commutes.
records.source_quote: Priority bus routes will result in more frequent service and less crowding as well as more efficient commutes for all users.

records.summary: States priority bus routes are a step toward supporting Toronto suburbs historically underserved by transit but reliant on it.
records.source_quote: This is a huge step towards supporting the Toronto suburbs that have been historically underserved by transit but heavily rely on it to get around.

records.summary: States that community safety is top of mind for residents with fall and back to school underway.
records.source_quote: With fall upon us and back to school well underway, a lot of us are thinking about safety in the community.

records.summary: Acknowledges community conversations about racism experienced by Black, Indigenous and People of Colour residents.
records.source_quote: the difficult but important conversations we have been having as a community around racism experienced by Black, Indigenous and People of Colour (BIPOC) residents

records.event_label: Community Safety Town Hall (virtual)
records.source_quote: I would like to invite you to a community safety town hall with me and Superintendent Reuben Stroble from Toronto Police Services, 55 Division. The meeting will be held virtually on Wednesday, October 7th from 6:30 pm to 8:30 pm.

records.summary: Supports ranked ballot voting as a step toward a more representative democracy in Toronto.
records.source_quote: Ranked ballot voting is an important step towards a democracy that is more representative of our diversity.

records.summary: States the current voting status quo is not working for thousands of Torontonians and rejects 'if it ain't broke, don't fix it' framing.
records.source_quote: "If it ain't broke, don't fix it" is an acceptance of the status quo that is not working for thousands of Torontonians.

records.summary: Observes that cities across the globe are adopting ranked ballot voting and benefiting, and Toronto should join them.
records.source_quote: Cities across the globe are adopting this system and reaping the benefits that come with it. We should join them and take the steps towards a more representative democracy.

records.summary: Supports protecting small businesses from evictions and reducing pressures from rising insurance costs as part of COVID response.
records.source_quote: protecting mom and pops from evictions, and reducing the pressures of rising insurance costs

records.summary: Contributed recommendations via Mayor Tory's COVID task force that were included in the Mayor's five-point plan to support local businesses.
records.source_quote: Mayor Tory's five-point plan to support local businesses as cases rise, including my recommendations from his COVID task force on protecting mom and pops from evictions, and reducing the pressures of rising insurance costs.

records.summary: States municipalities do much of the heavy lifting on building housing but have the fewest tools to support it.
records.source_quote: Municipalities do much of the heavy lifting in building housing but have the fewest tools to support this.

records.summary: Calls for a new deal for Canadian municipalities with Provincial and Federal governments contributing their fair share toward housing.
records.source_quote: We need a new deal for Canadian municipalities that sees the Provincial and Federal government contribute their fair share towards housing residents.

records.summary: ActiveTO program extended through October, providing space for active transportation during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: A huge win for active transportation with the #ActiveTO program being extended through October!

records.summary: Supports ActiveTO, stating it has been a success and provides safe space for fresh air and exercise during the second wave.
records.source_quote: It's been a huge success and continuing to provide a safe space for folks to get fresh air and exercise as we enter the second wave is crucial.

records.summary: States the ActiveTO program has been a success and that providing safe space for outdoor exercise during the second wave of COVID-19 is crucial.
records.source_quote: A huge win for active transportation with the #ActiveTO program being extended into October! It's been a huge success and continuing to provide a safe space for folks to get fresh air and exercise as we enter the second wave is crucial.

records.summary: States urgent action is needed to protect the climate and calls for further investments and commitment from all levels of government toward a sustainable society.
records.source_quote: Urgent action is needed to protect our climate and ensure we leave a livable world for generations to come. We need further investments into creating a truly sustainable society and commitment from all levels of government to make a change.

records.summary: States that Above Guideline Rent Increases threaten housing affordability for many Toronto residents.
records.source_quote: Above Guideline Rent Increases (AGIs) threaten to make that unaffordable for many.

records.summary: Supports asking the Province to close the AGI loophole, in keeping with the spirit of the 2021 rent freeze.
records.source_quote: In keeping with the spirit of the 2021 rent freeze, we’re asking the Province to close the AGI loophole.

records.summary: Asked the Province to close the Above Guideline Rent Increase (AGI) loophole.
records.source_quote: we’re asking the Province to close the AGI loophole

records.summary: Condemns the discovery of nooses at Michael Garron Hospital construction site as anti-Black racism with no place in the East End.
records.source_quote: I am disgusted by the recent discovery of two more nooses on a construction site @michaelgarronhospital. This is a disgusting display of Anti-Black racism and has no place in the East End.

records.summary: States that Toronto's diversity makes the city an incredible place and that work remains to ensure no one experiences racism.
records.source_quote: Our diversity is one of the many things that make this city an incredible place to live. Blatant hatred like this is a stark reminder that we have much work to do to ensuring that no one has to experience racism in our city.

records.quote_text: The East End stands with the victims of these horrific incidents.
records.speaker: Brad Bradford

records.summary: States the PRESTO system rollout was flawed but the city needs to move forward and implement changes.
records.source_quote: The rollout of the PRESTO system was not perfect... While the rollout was flawed, we need to move forward and implement the changes that will keep our transit system world class.

records.summary: Supports modernizing the fare system to allow open payments and account-based technology.
records.source_quote: 💳 Modernize the system to allow open payments and account-based technology

records.summary: Supports giving the TTC a role in selecting providers of the back-end technology to improve user experience.
records.source_quote: 🧰 The TTC will have a role in selecting providers of the back-end technology, improving user experience

records.summary: TTC negotiated a new agreement with Metrolinx giving the TTC more input into PRESTO implementation, coming to the TTC Board.
records.source_quote: The #TTC have been working out a new agreement with @metrolinx that will give us more input to the process, coming to the Board on Thursday.

records.summary: States the pandemic has highlighted cracks in the housing system and that these committee steps are crucial to recovery.
records.source_quote: The pandemic has highlighted the cracks in our housing system and these steps are crucial as we look towards our recovery.

records.summary: Planning and Housing Committee advanced an implementation plan for the 10-year housing strategy.
records.source_quote: Implementation plan for our 10 year #housing strategy

records.summary: Planning and Housing Committee advanced a new income-based definition for affordable housing.
records.source_quote: New income-based definition for affordable housing

records.summary: Planning and Housing Committee advanced the next step to require affordable housing in new developments.
records.source_quote: Next step to require affordable housing in new developments

records.summary: Promotes Cycle Toronto's Ride for Safe Streets to raise awareness for road safety.
records.source_quote: The #RideForSafeStreets with @cycletoronto is on now! Head online to register yourself or your social bubble, choose your route, and help raise awareness for road safety.

records.event_label: Ride for Safe Streets (Cycle Toronto)
records.source_quote: The #RideForSafeStreets with @cycletoronto is on now!

records.summary: Bringing measures to council including accessible loading zones on Kingston and Main, parking amendments on Kingston/Vent or/Rumney, compulsory stop controls on Keystone and Cedarvale, and realigning permit parking north of the Danforth.
records.source_quote: Here are the measures I'm bringing to council today: Adding accessible loading zones on Kingston and Main; Parking amendments on Kingston, Vent or, and Rumney; Compulsory stop controls on Keystone and Cedarvale; Realigning permit parking north of the Danforth

records.pledge_text: More road safety measures to come following the current package brought to council.
records.source_quote: Important steps to protecting all road users, with more coming soon!

records.summary: States road safety is top of mind as people return to work and school, and that active transportation users must be protected however they choose to get around.
records.source_quote: As folks go back to work and kids are heading back to school, road safety is top of mind. Active transportation is being rediscovered by many and it's crucial that they're protected, however they choose to get around.

records.summary: States intergovernmental partnerships with federal and provincial governments are necessary for an equitable solution to the housing crisis.
records.source_quote: Intergovernmental partnerships are critical to relieving pressure on our housing and shelter system. Support from federal (@justinpjtrudeau @chrystiafreeland @ahmeddhussen @cmhc_prez) and provincial (@fordnationdougford @steveclarkmpp) partners will be necessary for an equitable solution to the housing crisis.

records.summary: States the COVID-19 pandemic shows the need to accelerate the HousingTO 10-year action plan and shift toward permanent solutions to homelessness rather than reactive emergency measures.
records.source_quote: The COVID-19 pandemic has shown that we need to accelerate the actions of the HousingTO 10-year action plan. These 3,000 units will not only help us recover safely, but show the change towards permanent, sustainable solutions to homelessness rather than reactive, emergency measures.

records.summary: Announces the City's COVID-19 Housing and Homeless Recovery Plan to fast-track 3,000 permanent, affordable homes in 24 months.
records.source_quote: The City just released it's COVID-19 Housing and Homeless Recovery Plan to fast-track 3,000 permanent, affordable homes in 24 months.

records.summary: States that proactive, creative responses supporting small businesses are what communities expect from local government during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: This is the kind of proactive, creative response communities expect from their local government, especially at a time like this.

records.summary: Expanded patio heater permissions citywide, creating simplified rules to extend patio season and support restaurants during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: we've expanded patio heater permissions for patios across the city. The new permissions create a set of simplified rules that maintain safety and help extend patio season to support business.

records.summary: Worked with the Toronto Association of Business Improvement Areas and Mayor John Tory, gathering feedback from hundreds of small businesses during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: Working closely with the Toronto Association of Business Improvement Areas and Mayor @johntory - I've been listening to feedback from hundreds of small businesses to get through the pandemic.

records.summary: States that 'missing middle' housing is a crucial planning tool to expand housing options and improve affordability in Toronto.
records.source_quote: It's a crucial planning tool that will allow for more housing options in our communities and improve affordability for Torontonians.

records.summary: States that thoughtful policy changes like missing middle housing are necessary to address Toronto's housing crisis.
records.source_quote: These are the kinds of thoughtful policy changes that are necessary to address the housing crisis in Toronto.

records.summary: States that small business recovery must remain a priority alongside back-to-school focus.
records.source_quote: While we're rightly focused on back to school today, we can't lose sight of the small business recovery.

records.summary: Observes that Ontario's commercial eviction moratorium expired last month and rent relief is being extended piecemeal after rent was due.
records.source_quote: Ontario's commercial eviction moratorium expired last month and the rent relief program is being extended piecemeal again, over a week after rent is due.

records.summary: Calls for a decisive main street recovery plan involving federal, provincial, and municipal governments doubling down on early pandemic commitments.
records.source_quote: Our main streets need a decisive plan for recovery. It's going to take Feds... and Prov... working with the City... doubling down on the important commitments that were made early on during the pandemic.

records.event_label: The Beach #PickMeUp
records.source_quote: Coming up on September 20th! Join myself and @thetiffanypratt for The Beach #PickMeUp! Spend some time with the community, help to beautify our public spaces

records.summary: States the Danforth active transportation project is a strong start but more work remains.
records.source_quote: This project is a fantastic start, but more work remains to be done.

records.summary: Highlights work being done to support small businesses on the Danforth.
records.source_quote: speak with neighbours about the work being done to support small businesses and expand our active transportation network

records.event_label: Destination Danforth
records.source_quote: Mayor @JohnTory joined me on #DestinationDanforth to speak with neighbours about the work being done to support small businesses and expand our active transportation network.

records.summary: States that fears about urban interventions like these projects are largely unwarranted and the benefits are real, with residents asking for more.
records.source_quote: A lot of the fear-mongering that's associated with these sorts of projects isn't warranted, and the benefits are real. What I'm hearing, consistently, is people calling for more of these urban interventions.

records.quote_text: A lot of the fear-mongering that's associated with these sorts of projects isn't warranted, and the benefits are real. What I'm hearing, consistently, is people calling for more of these urban interventions.
records.speaker: Brad Bradford

records.summary: States that the pandemic has highlighted the importance of a digital presence for local businesses.
records.source_quote: The pandemic has highlighted the importance of a digital presence for our local businesses.

records.summary: Supports the expansion of the Digital Main Street program to help Toronto small businesses adapt.
records.source_quote: This expansion of the Digital Main Street program will help many Toronto mom-and-pops future proof their businesses and adapt to these constantly changing times.

records.summary: States Destination Danforth aims to bring people back to the community and safely support local small businesses.
records.source_quote: #DestinationDanforth is about bringing folks back into the community and supporting our local mom-and-pops safely.

records.summary: Notes new changes on the Danforth including street patios, 24/7 parking, and a protected cycle track.
records.source_quote: Lots of new changes, with street patios, 24/7 parking, and a protected cycle track.

records.summary: States that BIAs play an important role in communities and supporting local businesses, especially during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: BIA's play an incredibly important role in our communities and work tirelessly to support local businesses. This has never been more clear than during the pandemic.

records.summary: Supports The Beach Village BIA's expansion to help local mom-and-pop businesses recover.
records.source_quote: I wholeheartedly support The Beach Village BIA (@makewaves.to) in their expansion as they work to help our mom-and-pops recover.

records.summary: States that agile decision making is crucial during the pandemic.
records.source_quote: agile decision making is crucial during this pandemic

records.summary: Brought a motion, passed by Council, to accelerate the expansion process for The Beach Village BIA.
records.source_quote: I’m thankful to my Council colleagues for passing my motion to accelerate this process

records.summary: States investments in transit are critical for the sustainability of the TTC after pandemic pressures and to Toronto's recovery.
records.source_quote: These investments are especially critical for transit and the sustainability of our system after the immense pressure it was under as a result of the pandemic. The #TTC will be critical to our recovery and this funding will help to keep Toronto moving.

records.summary: States the time for action on policing and structural anti-racism is now.
records.source_quote: The time for action on policing and structural anti-Racism is now.

records.summary: Supports Mayor Tory's 81 recommendations to the Toronto Police board as following through on Council's commitment to action on anti-Black racism.
records.source_quote: Mayor Tory is bringing 81 recommendations to the Toronto Police board next week, making sweeping changes to Toronto's policing. These changes follow through on Council's commitment to pragmatically progressive action on anti-Black racism.

records.summary: References nearly 40 recommendations on policing/anti-racism passed by Toronto City Council in June.
records.source_quote: Following the nearly 40 recommendations passed by City Council in June

records.summary: Announced an online public consultation survey, open until August 18, on planned improvements to Ivan Forrest Gardens.
records.source_quote: Improvements are coming to the Ivan Forrest Gardens and we want to hear your thoughts on what changes are needed! An online survey is available until Tuesday, August 18th, to collect your feedback.

records.summary: Provides update on Destination Danforth Phase 3 construction, noting lane markings for bike lanes are nearly complete.
records.source_quote: #DestinationDanforth construction update - lane markings for Phase 3 are nearly done! Work to remove existing marks and paint the markings for bike lanes will finish tonight.

records.event_label: Community accessibility meeting on Destination Danforth
records.source_quote: Met with community members and City staff this morning to learn more about how we can improve accessibility on #DestinationDanforth. Thanks to Hema Murdock for organizing the meeting and sharing her thoughts and feedback.

records.summary: States municipalities deliver critical services but have the fewest financial tools to pay for them, leaving them vulnerable to shocks.
records.source_quote: despite the extensive breadth and scope of services we're expected to deliver, we are the least equipped with the financial tools and mechanisms to pay for them. Years of successive downloading, shrugging off responsibility and putting it on the back of property taxes and user fees, means we are particularly vulnerable to these sort of shocks and stresses.

records.summary: States municipal government is closest to people and does the heavy lifting of delivering critical day-to-day services.
records.source_quote: This branch of government is closest to people and does the heavy lifting, delivering critical services that folks rely on in their day-to-day lives.

records.pledge_text: Will continue to push and advocate for a New Deal for Cities.
records.source_quote: I'll continue to push and advocate for a New Deal for Cities.
records.specifics: Advocacy for a 'New Deal for Cities' to address municipal financial tools/funding.

records.summary: States that maintaining a healthy Toronto economy is crucial to Canada's long-term economic health.
records.source_quote: Maintaining a healthy economy in Toronto is crucial to the long-term economic health of Canada.

records.summary: Welcomes recent funding announcements as an investment to minimize fallout from the COVID-19 pandemic.
records.source_quote: The recent funding announcements are a very welcome investment to ensuring minimal fallout from the #COVID19 pandemic.

records.pledge_text: Commits to working with government partners to reach solutions on COVID-19 economic funding.
records.source_quote: Looking forward to seeing more details on this funding and working with our government partners to reach solutions!

records.summary: States residents should continue distancing from those outside their social circle and wear masks when distancing isn't possible as Toronto enters Stage 3 reopening.
records.source_quote: Toronto will be entering Stage 3 at 12:01am on Friday, July 31st! We've done a great job at stopping the spread, but we can't ease off now. Remember to keep your distance from those not in your social circle, and wear a mask whenever distancing isn't possible!

records.summary: States that priority bus lanes will shorten commutes, increase service frequency, and save money, benefiting frontline workers who rely on TTC buses.
records.source_quote: Expediting priority bus lanes will shorten these commutes, result in more frequent service, and save money.

records.summary: Observes that not everyone can work from home and that TTC buses are a crucial component of frontline workers' commutes.
records.source_quote: Not everyone has the option to work from home. For those who are working on the frontlines, #TTC buses are a crucial component of their commute.

records.summary: Phase 2 of Destination Danforth construction nearing completion; lane markings to be done by next day, physical separation by Friday.
records.source_quote: Phase 2 of the #DestinationDanforth construction is nearly complete! All lane markings will be implemented by tomorrow, with the installation of physical separation expected to be completed by Friday.

records.summary: States the restaurant and hospitality sector has had a tough few months and encourages residents to support local Danforth businesses.
records.source_quote: It's been a tough few months for the restaurant and hospitality sector, now's your chance to show them some #DanforthLove and enjoy the beginning of #DestinationDanforth!

records.summary: Announces launch of expanded patio program on the Danforth ('Destination Danforth') starting Saturday, with more locations rolling out further east in coming weeks.
records.source_quote: Sneak peek: here's your patio menu on the brand new Danforth starting Saturday night! More locations are coming further east in the next couple of weeks.

records.summary: Announces Phase 1 of Destination Danforth construction completing and Phase 2 (Jones to Woodbine) beginning, running 24/7 for roughly one week.
records.source_quote: Phase 1 of #DestinationDanforth construction will complete this afternoon, and Phase 2 (Jones to Woodbine) begins tonight! The construction will take roughly one week working 24/7.

records.summary: Supports Destination Danforth changes including expanded patio space, 24/7 parking, art installations, and a protected bike lane.
records.source_quote: We'll have more space for patios, more parking available 24/7, art installations, and a protected bike lane.

records.summary: Supports a protected bike lane on the Danforth as part of Destination Danforth.
records.source_quote: more parking available 24/7, art installations, and a protected bike lane

records.summary: Supports the Destination Danforth project with painted buffers and forthcoming physical separation for cycling infrastructure.
records.source_quote: First steps are being taken towards #DestinationDanforth! Painted buffers with different colours for our local BIAs, with physical separation coming soon. This has been a long time coming - can't wait to see it completed.

records.summary: Painted buffers installed on the Danforth as first steps of Destination Danforth, with physical separation to follow.
records.source_quote: First steps are being taken towards #DestinationDanforth! Painted buffers with different colours for our local BIAs, with physical separation coming soon.

records.summary: States that neighbourhood-specific housing plans will be more successful than a one-size-fits-all solution for Toronto's housing needs.
records.source_quote: There are hundreds of neighbourhoods in Toronto. Each of these neighbourhoods have different needs for housing. A plan specific to each area will be much more successful than a "one-size-fits-all" solution.

records.summary: States that tough conversations and hard work are needed to address housing inequality in Toronto.
records.source_quote: Tough conversations and hard work are needed to address housing inequality in Toronto.

records.summary: States that resident feedback as local experts is crucial to housing planning.
records.source_quote: This feedback as local experts is crucial.

records.summary: Consulted residents about the Missing Middle pilot coming to Beaches-East York; their input fed into the study and influenced the pilot's design.
records.source_quote: Earlier this year, I talked to residents about the Missing Middle pilot coming to #BEY later this year. Their input directly fed into the study and influenced the design of the pilot.

records.summary: States that wearing masks in enclosed public spaces is one of the most important things people can do to keep their community safe and stop the spread.
records.source_quote: Remember that masks are now required in enclosed public spaces! It's one of the most important things you can do to keep your community safe and stop the spread.

records.summary: Handed out masks to TTC riders at Woodbine station as part of a 1 million mask distribution initiative.
records.source_quote: Great morning at Woodbine station handing out masks for #TTC riders. 1 million masks will be handed out to keep Torontonians safe and support transit equity.

records.event_label: Mask handout for TTC riders
records.topic_focus: transit safety and mask distribution during COVID-19
records.source_quote: Great morning at Woodbine station handing out masks for #TTC riders.

records.summary: States that distributing masks to TTC riders supports rider safety and transit equity.
records.source_quote: 1 million masks will be handed out to keep Torontonians safe and support transit equity.

records.summary: States that surface transit is vital and priority routes are needed to connect historically underserved communities.
records.source_quote: Our surface transit is vital and these priority routes are needed to connect communities that have been historically underserved.

records.summary: Expediting the TTC bus priority route on Eglinton, with implementation planned for Fall.
records.source_quote: We're expediting the #TTC bus priority route on Eglinton, with implementation planned for Fall.

records.summary: States that wearing a face covering is one of the most important steps to stop the spread of COVID-19.
records.source_quote: Wearing a face covering is one of the most important steps you can take to stop the spread of #COVID19.

records.summary: Notes that a new by-law requiring masks in enclosed spaces takes effect today, with requirements for individuals and businesses.
records.source_quote: Masks are now required in enclosed spaces, starting today.

records.summary: States he will support both the Mayor's motions on anti-Black racism and police reform, and the motions for systemic change in policing put forward by Councillor Matlow and others.
records.source_quote: I'll be supporting both sets of motions on anti-Black racism and the police budget: the concrete steps to bring long overdue reform put forward by the Mayor, and the motions in solidarity for systemic change in policing put forward by Councillors Matlow and several others.

records.summary: Announced intent to vote in support of motions on anti-Black racism and police budget reform at City Council.
records.source_quote: As we come to the end of this debate, I'll be supporting both sets of motions on anti-Black racism and the police budget

records.summary: States that infrastructure investments on the Danforth are important to restoring consumer confidence as the economy reopens.
records.source_quote: These investments in our infrastructure are important to restoring consumer confidence as our economy continues to reopen.

records.summary: States that conduct at Woodbine Beach over the prior two weekends — including disregard for physical distancing and littering — was unacceptable.
records.source_quote: The situation we've seen at the Beach over the last two weekends is completely unacceptable. The level of disregard we saw, not only for physical distancing but even the basics of picking up after yourself, was shocking.

DXz7S9euglk.caption:
I love this city and I’m running for Mayor because Toronto deserves better.

Safer streets, less gridlock, and a city that works again.

I’m focused on three priorities: crime, congestion, and costs.

Let’s build a city we can be proud of.

DX2ITbHjjzF.caption:
Spent some time this afternoon at the Wychwood Barns Farmers Market and Quilt Show today with @stephaniesmythtsp.

A treasured community spot for neighbours and families. I’m inspired by the people I met today, and grateful for the talent and gifts they give our city.

DX116uejXjn.caption:
Started the morning in Scarborough with chai, coffee, and an honest conversation with neighbours about what our city needs to get right, including better transit for Scarborough. 

Thank you to former MPP Brad Duguid for joining, and to Khazana for the warm welcome.

DX1rX3cN-Nj.caption: Happy to have the support of the Hon. John McKay, who served Scarborough Guildwood in Parliament for nearly 30 years. Watch his message.

DXzdph5jnnR.caption:
This account will now be where I share updates from my campaign for Mayor of Toronto.

For my work as your Councillor in Beaches-East York, you can continue to follow along at @beybradford.

DXw_o1TifLm.caption:
This week has been about community, leadership, and the people shaping Toronto’s future.

I was honoured to attend a Shabbat dinner at the Collective Makon — a great chance to slow down and connect. Thank you to Rebecca for the warm welcome and for bringing people together.

Shovels hit the ground at 5507 Dundas Street West, an important step forward on much-needed housing. With 259 new purpose-built rental homes, this is the kind of project Toronto needs more of. Thank you to everyone who helped get it there.

At Chabad on Bayview, the graduating class of the leadership program showed what real leadership looks like. In a moment when it matters more than ever, young people are choosing to stand up, take responsibility, and lead with courage.

I heard from many residents across the city who care deeply about where Toronto is headed. Thank you to Marla, Aviva, Yaear, Sean, Sara, Jacquie, Stacey, Mark, and Joe for hosting these important conversations, and to everyone who came out to share their perspectives and ideas.

DXufqImlfOt.caption:
Last summer, residents were clear: dangerous jet ski activity at Woodbine Beach had to stop.

I brought forward a motion to create a no-go zone, and it passed unanimously at Council. 

With a motorized watercraft ban coming to Woodbine and Cherry beaches this summer, it needs to be clearly marked, strongly enforced, and focused on what matters: keeping people safe.

I will keep pushing for buoys, enforcement, and tangible results for our waterfront.

Share this to help spread the word before summer hits.

DXsVjn3lGjq.caption:
What gives me hope? Torontonians do. The folks who show up every day to build our great city.

But right now, city leadership isn’t holding up its end of the bargain.

We don't have to keep settling for mediocrity and managed decline. We can build a world class city that all of us can be proud of. We just need leadership as good as our people to do it.

Let's go.

DXsKhB1D26r.caption:
Breaking ground on projects that will shape the future of our communities is always meaningful. 🏗️

It was a pleasure joining Brad Bradford, Larry Blankenstein, and Stephen Marshall for this important groundbreaking. This development will bring new purpose-built rental housing and commercial space to Toronto, supporting growth, opportunity, and vibrant neighbourhood life across our city. 

#MPPMichelleCooper #EglintonLawrence #Ontario #Housing

DXpl18qCgFE.caption:
This weekend showed what happens when the basics break down — closed roads, closed transit, and people stuck paying the price in lost time.

That’s the “time tax” Torontonians face every day — and it’s time City Hall starts planning better and delivering accountability.

DXmbu-mjQuq.caption:
My heart is with the Armenian community in Toronto and around the world in solemn remembrance of the 1.5 million Armenians systematically persecuted and killed beginning in 1915.

Armenian Genocide Remembrance Day honours the memory of those lost, pays tribute to the resilience and strength of survivors, and stands as a reminder to bring forward the truth so the world never forgets. In remembering this dark chapter of human history, we pledge to reject intolerance and hatred in every corner of society that we find it.

We are lucky in Toronto to have such a vibrant Armenian community who continue to meaningfully contribute to our great city. As the community gathers to observe this most solemn of memorials, I join you in standing against oppression in all its forms and pushing for a more peaceful and just future that we can all be proud of.

DXj5Yu1jWyd.caption:
This past week was a reminder that Toronto’s strength comes from the many communities that shape our city.

Bengali New Year celebrations took place at the Toronto Bangla School, where Jannatul and her team continue to bring people together, and keeping language and culture strong. We also marked the Nepali New Year alongside Srijansil Nepali Samaj, who have been supporting families and creating space for young people to stay rooted in their identity since 2015. This week, I joined he unveiling of a Heritage Toronto plaque at St. George’s Greek Orthodox Church, recognizing its role in Toronto’s early Greek community. Moments like these reflect the diversity and pride that define our city.

Toronto has one of the strongest tech and innovation hubs in the world, and that was clear at the spring social hosted by CMCC Global. A room full of builders and leaders focused on what it takes to grow, invest, and succeed here, and on how we make sure Toronto keeps up with its potential.

Across neighbourhoods, people continue to step up with ideas and a shared commitment to getting things right. Thanks to Oren, Mike, Saei, Cameron, Afshin, Maryam, Andrew, Bram, Ilana, Bradley, and Geoff for hosting these important conversations about the future of our city, and to everyone who came out and took part.

DXiEz2GDX03.caption:
A quick recap from this month’s Council — from transit in Scarborough to tickets for the FIFA Fan Fest, we had to clean up on the mayor’s missed commitments and shifting positions.

Toronto deserves better focus, better follow-through, and leadership that gets the basics right.

DXfZVpDDbXy.caption:
Mayor Chow promised families in Toronto a free FIFA Fan Fest. Then, she told fans to pay. Then, she flip flopped again. 

The pattern of confusion, poor execution and zero accountability when things go wrong needs to change at city hall. 

This summer, the only goal posts you should see changing is on the pitch - not coming from the Mayor’s Office telling you to pay for a free event.

DXc5lIFjQo_.caption:
Scarborough has waited long enough.

While billions move forward to other neighbourhoods, transit here is still stuck without funding. It’s unacceptable. It’s time to deliver real investment and for Mayor Chow to stop treating commuters in Scarborough like an afterthought.

DXaTGVNgQ7V.caption:
This project at 511 Kingston Road went from a stalled hole in the ground to 90 new homes, including 30 deeply affordable units.

This is what is looks like when we refuse to settle.

DXXFDckDmhp.caption:
A lot of the work police do happens out of sight, in moments most people never see and under circumstances that can change in an instant.

I spent Saturday night out on patrol with members of 51 Division to get a better look at that work firsthand. One of the most valuable parts of the evening was seeing how the Mobile Crisis Intervention Team responds alongside officers to support people experiencing mental health crises.

Thank you to Enis, Brian, and the officers at 51 Division, and across all divisions in Toronto, for putting themselves on the line every day to help keep Torontonians safe.

DXU7qKVlRsd.caption:
Sports like hockey bring people together, build confidence, and create lifelong friendships. 

Yesterday, I was proud to help celebrate a big milestone: 65 years of the Forest Hill Hockey Association! 

Thank you to the volunteers, coaches, and families who have put in the work over the years to help kids experience the power of sport, here and in neighborhoods right across the city.

DXUSg3sDnNk.caption:
Last night, Councillor @bradfordgrams joined our members at @tps51div for a ride-along, gaining firsthand insight into the critical work they do across the community.

The evening included an up-close look at our Mobile Crisis Intervention Teams and the vital support they provide to individuals experiencing mental health crises.

Thank you for taking the time to see this important work in action.

DXR8pQiDWDV.caption:
A big milestone this week at 511 Kingston Road, where we broke ground on a project that will turn a long-stalled hole in the ground into 90 new rental homes, including 30 affordable units. This one took real persistence to get moving, and it’s great to see it now moving forward with Cannect Homes, Streetcar Developments, Neighbours, and strong local partners.

That same community spirit was on display in North York, where residents rolled up their sleeves for shoreline cleanups and helped care for local green spaces. Thank you to everyone who took the time to pitch in and help keep these shared spaces clean.

I was also honoured to join the National Council of Canadian Tamils for their Grand Gala. The Tamil community continues to make a major contribution to Toronto through leadership in business, culture, and civic life, and it was a privilege to celebrate that alongside so many community leaders.

At City Hall, Toronto’s new Chief Congestion Officer stopped by to talk about one of the issues people raise most often: traffic. Toronto needs a serious plan to reduce gridlock and make it easier for people to move around the city.

And across Toronto, the conversations continued. Thank you to Carmen, Barbara, Anna, Sheldon, Sharlene, Murray, and Jonathan for bringing people together and creating space for thoughtful discussions about the future of our city.

DXPceKkGoHQ.caption:
If it feels like Toronto is getting dirtier, you’re not imagining it, and it matters.

Clean streets aren’t a luxury, they’re a basic standard, and it’s time City Hall gets back to focusing on what people see and experience every day.

DXNNYyaDSsq.caption:
Yesterday, I called out Mayor Chow’s plan to charge Toronto families $10 each for a festival that she promised would be free. For a family of five, that's $50 just to get through the gate.

Now, after the backlash, the mayor is scrambling to patch it with some free tickets. But this wouldn't have happened if she kept her promise of a free festival.

The point of a FIFA fan fest is that it belongs to the people. These celebrations should be open to everybody, not just the people who can afford the price of admission.

DXKu-UHDqz2.caption: This week, City Hall highlighted a “tree equity” policy — but while people are worried about crime, congestion, and the cost of living, the focus should be on the basics that actually impact daily life.

DXIUjKNjYHl.caption: This Vaisakhi, Sikh communities here in Toronto and around the world come together in prayer and celebration — a powerful reminder of the values of service, community, and resilience that continue to shape our city.

DXH5PTBFUSn.caption:
This morning, we gathered at City Hall to commemorate Yom HaShoah. On this day, we remember the six million Jews who were murdered simply for being Jewish. We reflect on the immense loss, the lives and communities that were destroyed, and the generations forever impacted by the Holocaust.

As we mark 81 years since the liberation of the Nazi concentration camps, we also honour the strength, resilience, and courage of those who survived. Their stories continue to bear witness, reminding us of the importance of remembrance, education, and standing against antisemitism and hatred in all its forms.

DXFF6rHDlAz.caption:
Yesterday was a special day for many families across Toronto celebrating Orthodox Easter. I had the chance to make a few stops in Parkview Hills and East York to mark the occasion with residents and share in a holiday rooted in faith, renewal, and time with loved ones. Thanks to Steve, Konstantinos, and Stefanos for hosting me. 

Wishing everyone who celebrated a happy Orthodox Easter!

DXC2M4tippP.caption: A better Toronto starts with all of us. Let’s keep our parks and neighbourhoods clean.

DW_xwiTDSVQ.caption:
These past days have been productive, rewarding, and a great time connecting with those who make Toronto work. 

I joined members and leaders of Toronto’s Eritrean community for an important conversation about our city where I got to hear their concerns about the rising cost of living, and what it takes to make Toronto a place where people can still build a life, raise a family, and pursue opportunity. Thank you to Jonathan for bringing everyone together, and to EriPMN and New6Soccer for helping create such a thoughtful and engaged discussion.

I also spent time in Danforth Village hearing directly from residents and local business owners about the day-to-day issues affecting the neighbourhood, and the improvements they want to see on their main street. These conversations matter because strong communities depend on clean, welcoming public spaces and local streets people can feel proud of.

Had a chance to sit down with Christine Hogarth in Alderwood for a conversation about local issues and the future of Toronto.

And across the city, the conversations kept going. Grateful to Elaine, Justein, Nicki, Simmy, Adam and Annie for helping bring people together and for creating space to talk about where Toronto needs to go next.

DW9omxgiiuh.caption:
The plan exists. What’s missing is the political will. 

Scarborough deserves the same urgency and the same transit that works.

DW6x_2yjv-x.caption:
People in Scarborough are tired of waiting. 

While billions are committed elsewhere, transit in Scarborough remains stalled and that’s not fair. It’s time to deliver real investment and respect people’s time.

DW2FRA0ANLp.caption: The Vacant Home Tax is supposed to free up housing, but instead it’s creating more confusion, more bureaucracy, and higher costs for homeowners.

DWzJp66CQV9.caption:
It was great to be out as a family at the annual Beaches Lions Easter Parade. 

For 60 years, it’s been a spring tradition, and it’s amazing to see the community spirit year after year.

Happy Easter to all!

DWv8kILDj9n.caption:
Happy Easter to everyone celebrating across Toronto.

It's a time for hope, renewal, and new beginnings. Wishing you and your family a joyful and peaceful weekend.

DWts0yWjUnF.caption:
Last week brought meaningful celebrations across Toronto, rooted in culture, tradition, and community. 

On the Danforth, blue and white were everywhere as Toronto’s Greek community came together to celebrate Greek Independence Day. From the parade on Sunday to a special gala the evening before, it was a proud celebration of heritage, culture, and the generations who have helped build this city.

Nowruz offered a chance for Iranians around the world to welcome the new year with hope, renewal, and time together. It was a privilege to celebrate in North York and mark the occasion alongside so many members of the Iranian community in Toronto. Thank you to Councillor Lily Cheng for organizing.

Passover also brought a meaningful opportunity to gather in reflection and tradition. Thank you to Sharlene and Sheldon for welcoming me into their home for the First Seder and for sharing such a special evening with warmth and generosity.

And across the city, residents continued to bring forward their ideas and their commitment to a better Toronto. Thank you to Adam, Eryn, and Nick for hosting these thoughtful conversations, and to everyone who came out to be part of them.

DWpQsyhDntz.caption:
The East York Hockey Association is the only minor hockey league in the world allowed to present a Stanley Cup replica - and that’s what we did this past weekend during Little Stanley Cup Day. 

For over 80 years, the league has been bringing kids in our community together through sportsmanship, teamwork and a love for hockey. 

Congrats to all the teams on a great season, and thanks to all the coaches and volunteers who make it happen!

DWmsbN3iipV.caption:
Chag Pesach Kasher V’Sameach.

As Jewish families gather to mark Passover, I’m reminded of the resilience and strength at the heart of this story, and especially today, I stand with Toronto’s Jewish community.

DWjaxtoCmxp.caption:
It was a true honour to join His Highness the Aga Khan at the Ismaili Centre for the inauguration of Generations Toronto. 

This community-focused development will bring affordable rental housing, long-term care, and support for seniors and families together in one place. It is yet another meaningful demonstration of how the Ismaili community has stepped forward to make Toronto a stronger and more compassionate city. 

As our city grows, we need more projects like this that innovate and bring together community, the private sector and all levels of government.

DWhiBdhjRbG.caption:
A big step forward for TTC safety! City Council has approved my motion to expand police presence, improve station conditions, and move forward on platform doors.

Too many riders don’t feel safe today and now the work begins to restore confidence and make transit something Torontonians can rely on again.

DWe8o5mEQ9x.caption: A great day on the Danforth celebrating Greek Independence Day - incredible energy, strong community spirit, and a proud reminder of the history, culture, and contributions of Toronto’s Greek community.

DWb4LOVDWwL.caption:
Started this morning meeting the Easter Bunny with the @centre55toronto Easter Egg Hunt! 🐰 🐣 

A few other highlights from the week:

Meeting with students from Adam Beck JPS who stopped by during Council and got a firsthand look at local government in action.

Welcoming Mayor Vânia Ferreira of Praia da Vitória in the Azores. It was great to build on the strong ties between Portugal and Toronto. 

We also marked Bangladesh Independence Day, and celebrated the incredible contribution of Toronto’s Bangladeshi community to the life of our city.

The Passover reception at City Hall was a meaningful opportunity to come together around faith, tradition, and community. That spirit continued with a visit to Gesher Canada, where I had the chance to learn more about the work they do to support the community. 

There was some Toronto sports pride in the mix too, as we welcomed members of Canada’s Women’s Olympic hockey team (and Toronto Sceptre players!). A proud moment for the city and for women’s sport.

And beyond City Hall, the conversations continued. Residents, professionals, and community leaders brought forward their ideas, concerns, and hopes for the future of this city. Thank you to Shawn and The Creek for hosting in Scarborough, and to Robbie, Alex, and everyone else who helped bring people together across Toronto.

DWZyuhICoQQ.caption:
A big step forward for transit safety in Toronto.

My Safer TTC motion passed with unanimous support, 23-0. Now it’s time to deliver real, visible changes so riders can feel safe and confident getting where they need to go.

DWXXm8Yiazl.caption: I’m all in on Toronto - but it’s time to get back to basics and make the city work again.

DWU5JzJiHrx.caption:
Torontonians don’t need more excuses — they need safer transit. 

My plan is straightforward: police at every station, clear standards for cleanliness and lighting, and finally moving forward on platform doors. The time for delay is over — let’s get on with it.

DWRvajOlRmT.caption:
Today is Agnes Macphail Day, a chance to honour an East York legend and reflect on the legacy she left in public life.

Agnes Macphail was a trailblazer in Canadian politics whose courage, independence, and commitment to fairness continue to resonate today. In East York, her legacy also lives on through a long-standing tradition of recognizing individuals whose work strengthens the community and reflects the values she championed.

This past weekend at the East York Civic Centre, Dr. Blair Bigham was recognized as the 2026 recipient of the Agnes Macphail Award. Congratulations on this well-deserved honour. 👏

DWPZGCUFT_z.caption:
Torontonians aren’t being heard when they say they don’t feel safe on the TTC — and gaslighting them that everything is fine isn’t good enough.

It’s time for real action: visible police presence, enforced cleanliness and safety standards, and real accountability that restores confidence in our transit system.

DWM5ARvjZHd.caption: Joined hundreds of volunteers to fill boxes of Passover food for families in need at @ujafederation's Packing it Forward event — a powerful reminder of how we can come together and give back to support all members of our community.

DWKIJh8lcMK.caption:
Another week of important moments across Toronto.

The Hungarian community has contributed to Toronto’s economy and culture for decades, and the Hungarian-Canadian Business Awards Gala was a celebration of that entrepreneurship, leadership, and success, along with the strong ties that continue to grow between communities across our city.

That same spirit of people showing up for one another is alive on the Danforth, where Jim and Dahna at Wishy Washy Coin Laundry continue to make a real difference through their free laundry access program, offering practical support to neighbours facing hard times. Their important work is a powerful example of community care in action.

East York also marked a one-in-a-lifetime milestone as the East York Garden Club celebrated its 100th anniversary. It was a beautiful reminder of the traditions, volunteer spirit, and neighbourhood pride that have shaped East York for generations. Shoutout to Veronica for sharing great gardening tips, and to Joyce, who has been part of the club for 40 years and is also turning 100 this year! 

St. Patrick’s Day in Toronto always brings out the best spirit in the city. After a great parade, the celebrations continued at Minister Todd McCarthy’s St. Patrick’s night, bringing together public officials and community leaders for an evening that reflected the traditions and cultures that make Toronto one of the best places to be.

At City Hall, I met with Ilze Lacgalve from the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia. We had a thoughtful conversation that highlighted the value of strong international relationships and the opportunities these can create for Toronto.

Conversations across the city continue, and hearing from people who care deeply about Toronto’s future is always energizing. At U of T’s Law and Business Association, students brought real thoughtfulness and ambition to the conversation, and across Toronto, residents, professionals, and community members continue to bring forward the ideas and concerns that will help build a better city.

DWH7cx5AbI5.caption:
Nowruz marks the start of the new year for Persians around the world. 

While we begin this new year with heavy hearts, we celebrate the strength, resilience and hope that the new year brings, and remind ourselves that light always drowns out darkness. 

Nowruzetan Pirouz. 
Paayande Iran.

DWHLFbgjdFX.caption:
Eid is a time of celebration, reflection, gratitude, and community. 

This morning, I joined the Muslim community in Scarborough for an Eid prayer marking the end of Ramadan. It was a meaningful opportunity to be with community members, to listen to their aspirations and concerns and to recognize the traditions and values that bring people together across our great city.

Eid Mubarak to everyone celebrating across Toronto! ☪️

DWFOTgOCdsC.caption: I’m bringing forward real, immediate steps to restore safety and confidence on transit — because empty promises aren’t enough, and people deserve to feel safe getting where they need to go.

DWCaqVtCq70.caption:
Stopped by Brave Leather to see firsthand how their products are made — from raw leather to finished belts and bags — and to meet the incredible team behind it.

Proud to support a Toronto company that’s creating great jobs and exporting quality craftsmanship across Canada and around the world.

DV_trRPDqdJ.caption:
Happy St Patrick’s Day, Toronto! ☘️ 

We had a great day out at the St. Patrick’s Day Parade on Sunday — celebrating the traditions and community spirit that make Toronto so special.

DV9j5gKDfT8.caption:
Stopped by @tedreevehockey arena to meet Andrew Adair, the founder of @openiceinitiative an incredible youth-led program removing financial barriers so more kids can experience the game of hockey.

Great to see community leadership like this making sure every kid gets a chance to get on the ice.

DV6-R8gDgYG.caption:
Irish eyes were smiling! ☘️🇮🇪

Had a great time walking in the @stpatrickstoronto Parade today with my family, alongside the parade's Grand Marshal Todd McCarthy @toddmccarthydurham

DV4fO40kueM.caption:
Getting out to visit local businesses and community leaders this week was a great reminder of the talent, entrepreneurship, and civic pride that continue to drive Toronto forward.

At Brave Leather, I had the chance to learn more about what it takes to build and sustain a successful Canadian handcrafted manufacturer in our city.

That same spirit was clear at Nortown Air, where I heard directly from a long-standing family business about how City Hall can better support these job creators. 

With Nowruz just around the corner, I was honoured to attend the 2026 Persian Awards and recognize inspiring community leaders whose contributions continue to strengthen our city. Thank you to Rose and the Persian Awards team for a fantastic event.

I also met with Linda Carter to discuss how we can help the Ontario Black History Society find a new home in Toronto, and how to better recognize the contributions of Black Canadians to our city’s past, present and future.

Across Toronto, I continued having thoughtful conversations with people who care deeply about building a safer, more affordable, and better Toronto. Grateful to Romy, Jeremy, Aleks and Derrick for hosting me, and to everyone who took part in those conversations.

DV11FeuAKEG.caption:
One of my favourite moments from my conversation with @tessavirtue17 was hearing about the first time her son stepped onto the ice with her husband at their neighbourhood rink.

Sometimes the simplest moments become the memories you never forget.

DVzJnfTAZwm.caption:
Al Quds Day has become an annual platform for antisemitic hate and extremist rhetoric. In today’s climate, this raises serious public safety concerns.

I call on the City to take the necessary steps - up to and including an injunction - to cancel the demonstration.

DVylD0AkWQr.caption: @tessavirtue17 and I couldn't stop talking about what makes Toronto so great.

DVwdAnjFb0O.caption: Round two of the Toronto music quiz. Another five songs, another reminder that this city has produced some serious talent. Curious how many you got right.

DVwbTE8Fliq.caption:
One of the most decorated Olympic figure skaters in history. ⛸️ 
Canadian ice dancing legend Tessa Virtue joined Toronto City Councillor Brad Bradford on the ice at the Cricket Club this week for a conversation for his podcast. 
Just another special moment at the Cricket Club. 
#TheCricketClub #TessaVirtue #BradBradford #CricketPride

DVuIpP0k6XF.caption:
Had a great time at the @torontocricketclub with @tessavirtue17. We dusted off a few moves on the ice, and she reminded me that a little courage goes a long way — even when the execution still needs some work.

Stay tuned for our full conversation on @fortheloveof_to - out Thursday!

DVroVunldzD.caption: I had the honour of celebrating Lunar New Year with members of Toronto’s Chinese community. As we rang in the Year of the Fire Horse together, I was grateful for the chance to recognize the incredible contributions they make to our city and to celebrate the diversity that makes Toronto such a special place to call home.

DVo5jzxDgVg.caption:
Celebrated International Women’s Day with Kathryn, Briar, and Bronwyn by taking them all to their first @pwhl_sceptres game!

They loved cheering on some incredible athletes and it was great to see my girls getting inspired by the strong, talented women that are leaders on and off the ice.

GO SCEPTRES GO!

DVmN8OPDpY8.caption:
Another week of taking action 🏃 

The Toronto Prayer Breakfast brought together faith, civic, and community leaders from across the city for a morning of reflection, fellowship, and prayer. It was an honour to recognize the police officers, firefighters, and paramedics who serve our communities every day. 

I joined Tyler McLay’s Real Estate Forum in Etobicoke to talk about the future of Toronto’s housing market. The conversation focused on what matters most: affordability, supply, and how we build a city where people can still see a future for themselves.

The Scarborough Shooting Stars Foundation gala was a powerful reminder of what happens when young people are given real support and opportunity. Across Scarborough and the GTA, this work is opening doors, building confidence, and shaping brighter futures. 

I was happy to be back at the Digital Asset Summit. The conversation was all about innovation, Canadian talent, and Toronto’s future. Our city has the people, ideas, and entrepreneurial energy to lead, but that only happens when leadership backs local talent and embraces new ideas. Thanks to Landon and Web3 Toronto for the invitation.

Walking back into York and the Schulich School of Business brought a lot back for me. I spoke with students in the Master of Real Estate and Infrastructure program about housing, city-building, and what it takes to move ideas into action at City Hall. We also recorded a podcast, so stay tuned for a broader conversation about Toronto’s future.

Across Toronto, I’ve been sitting down to listen to people who care deeply about where our city is headed. These conversations were thoughtful, honest, and grounded in both the challenges people are feeling and the opportunities ahead. Grateful to Jessica, Evan, Brian, Kat, and Oren for hosting me and bringing people together.

DVloXWPDe6p.caption:
More bullets were fired at Jewish synagogues last night, on Shabbat, including Shaarei Shomayim in North York. 

I am horrified and outraged. I joined them earlier this week for Purim - a joyful celebration of the strength and survival of the Jewish people. To see their place of worship targeted in this cowardly, antisemitic attack disgusts me. 

These photos are of the gunfire damage at The BAYT in Thornhill, which also happened last night.

Toronto Police will have an enhanced presence outside places of worship, but it’s long past time for real action to build a city where that isn’t required. Where hateful acts like this are prevented, and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.

About Last Night…..

A packed house of concerned voters braved the cold (and snow)  to hear Mayoral Candidate and Councillor of Beaches - East York Brad Bradford speak about his vision for the City of Toronto. He listened to our question ls and concerns from crime to traffic. He answered thoughtfully and with clear direction. 

I met Brad over a year ago. He was gracious enough to accept an invite to be on my podcast. 

I was expecting a politician. Vague answers. No commitment. Word Salads. 

Instead I met a genuine citizen. A father. A husband. A man who knows that Toronto can be better than it is. And wants to be the person who will make that happen. 

The fall election will be here before you know it. Inform yourself with facts. Think of the future of this city. Toronto needs a change! 

I know I will on voting day as I endorse Brad Bradford for Mayor 

If you are interested in holding your own event, DM me and I will connect you with his team

DScgmZfjTg0.caption:
The most basic job of a government is to keep their citizens safe. And in this, Toronto City Hall has failed. Violent incidents on Toronto area transit are up 127% since 2015. Ridership is down as a result. 

Getting the basics right means putting forward a clear, coordinated and accountable transit safety strategy designed to outlaw the crime plaguing our transit systems and restore the peace-of-mind riders used to be able to expect. 

As a city planner, I know how to get the job done. As a dad, I know why it’s important. It’s time to make our transit system safe. Share if you’re with me.👆

DSabj0Mjkvw.caption:
At City Hall, I pushed to double the first-time homebuyer rebate instead of piling on yet another tax increase.

My proposal was voted down, while the Mayor’s luxury home tax hike moved forward — a decision that does little to help families trying to build equity and get into the housing market.

Toronto needs practical, common-sense solutions that focus on affordability and opportunity, not more taxes layered onto a system that already isn’t working for too many people. I’ll keep making that case.

Young families in our city are counting on their leaders to fight for their dream of home ownership. They can count on me to never back down.
