CH06QJ7BHgY.caption:
Going into lockdown is a major blow but it's our only choice to fight this long-term. We have to match the weight of this step with the depth of our support for those affected, starting with reinstating the moratorium on evictions for families & small businesses #onpoli

These are some steps governments can take immediately:

▪️The Province can stop evictions for families and businesses, and help people pay the rent (the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy and Canada Emergency Rent Subsidy for small business were just approved in parliament today)
▪️The Feds and Province can double down on funding commitments for sectors that have been most heavily impacted, especially health, wellness and fitness studios to help them keep the lights on. The Province has announced a doubling in small business funding taking the relief budget to $600 million. 
▪️Move forward meaningfully on our commitments to rebuild better with steps like accelerating roll-out of our rapid transit network like bus priority corridors (City) and addressing systemic policy issues like commercial tax assessments (City and Province). 

We've been here and we know that the most important thing for all governments is to reassure communities and take action to build back better after. Feds, Provinces and Cities need to align, and have funding committed from the levels of government that have the best ability to pay.

CH0lP80BFRH.caption:
We have to live and experience the city differently this winter. The City's responding to advocacy from across the city and planning to double winter washroom access: 79 facilities in 64 locations will help us stay safe and healthy.

Getting outdoors for fresh air and some sunlight will be crucial for our mental and physical health this winter. This change will incentivize folks to get outside, safely, and facilitate the continued use of our beautiful parks through the winter.

CHyL5MWh5RJ.caption:
Electric vehicles will play a critical role in meeting our emission goals across the City. Recent studies have shown that the biggest barrier to EV ownership is a lack of access to convenient charging stations. Recently we unveiled the EV Charging Station pilot with 17 charging stations around Toronto. This is a great first step, but more work needs to be done.

Front yard parking, or parking pads, would provide a place for folks to charge their vehicle right in front of their home. There are strict environmental regulations in place for front yard parking, with requirements for permeable paving materials and protecting trees.

Unfortunately, the process to apply for front yard parking is broken. People frequently skirt around the process through appeal boards in order to achieve their desired outcome. We need a pragmatic approach to incentivize EV use in our neighbourhoods. This report we'll be getting back will address many of the concerns and help us move into the 21st century together.

CHbVwUfhwx9.caption:
Dr. de Villa is making the  extremely difficult, but correct, decision to bring in more restrictions in Toronto, starting Saturday. These closures put even further pressure on businesses that have been struggling throughout the pandemic and urgent support is needed. While public health comes first, we need to be looking at the long-term recovery of our main streets as well.

A good start would be addressing problems that have plagued businesses long before the pandemic. We need new commercial tax bands to prevent neighbourhood stores being taxed the same as an office tower. We need further protection for commercial tenants to protect against unscrupulous landlords. There are also opportunities for the City to incentivize entrepreneurs with lower start-up costs. Our economic recovery will run through main street and we need to do everything we can to protect our mom-and-pops through another lockdown.

I know that these closures are hard and they’re taking a toll on all of us. But the only way through this is by staying laser focused on beating this thing. We’ll get through this together.

I should be clear, nothing has changed in terms of the requirements to have permeable paving and to protect trees. The environmental considerations have to come first and foremost. This is a big step forward to incentivizing electric vehicle ownership to meet our climate goals.

In tandem with this, we have some new EV chargers in the neighbourhood! One station is at Bowmore/Eastwood with another opening on Westlake next weekend. We have a long way to go to meet our climate goals - enabling EV ownership will play a significant part.

CGz7Ivbhrou.caption:
Restaurants, cafes, and bars have been having a tough time throughout the pandemic. Many folks are turning to delivery apps like Uber Eats or Door Dash to help support these local businesses while we can't dine indoors. However, many of these apps have significant fees that restaurants must pay. This hurts their bottom line and makes the margins even more thin.

Some popular meal service apps charge restaurants commissions as high as 35%. With local businesses hurting so badly right now, we should be tackling this like LA, New York and Seattle have. Thanks to Councillor @michael.ford.to for bringing the issue forward to Council this week!

CGximMKBFqG.caption:
Road safety is my top local priority and throughout the pandemic I’ve been working with residents to introduce new traffic calming measures throughout the neighbourhood. However, City by-laws require a polling process in order to introduce these measures on residential streets. With large backlogs due to the COVID-19 pandemic, I’m working directly with the community to run polls on road safety interventions so that our efforts to make our streets safer don’t fall behind.

On my website is a digital list of community polls which can be used to show support. Check out bradbradford.ca/petitions (link in bio) for more information and a list of active polls. If you don’t see your street listed but think some traffic calming is needed - please reach out! I can always be contacted at Councillor_Bradford.ca or through my social media profiles.

CGurGZ3hxpR.caption:
Reese Fallon's life was tragically cut short in the 2018 Danforth shooting. She was an optimist and advocate for change - two qualities that reflect the best of our community. We want to honour her short but impactful time with us by naming a laneway after her.

The proposed location is south of Gerrard and east of Wayland. This location was chosen because of the proximity to her home, her schools, and her friends. It will provide a place for loved ones to honour her memory.

Neighbour support is needed to officially rename a laneway in Toronto. I started an online petition to gather this support. Please visit my website at bradbradford.ca/reeselane (link in bio) for more information or to sign the petition.

CGiSMSVhoGK.caption:
Emotional afternoon canvassing for neighbour support to name a laneway in memory of Reese Fallon, one of the two victims whose life was tragically cut short in the Danforth Shooting on July 22, 2018.

Reese  lived with her family in our East End community. At 18, she had just graduated from Malvern Collegiate Institute and planned to go into the Nursing program at McMaster University when she and 10-year-old Julianna Kozis, were killed.

This tragic loss in our community is still hard to fathom and her care and passion are sorely missed. 

Reese’s memory, of course, lives on through our caring community.  With her family, we would like to name a Laneway after her. This would be a legacy to her short yet impactful time among us. The proposed location is close to her home, the schools that she attended and to the many friends who cherished her. Many in the community would appreciate an opportunity to remember Reese and to perhaps feel her presence through a namesake location. 

You can add your support at bradbradford.ca/reeselane.

CGiACwTBlkT.caption:
As the Small Business lead for Mayor @johntory’s Economic Support and Recovery Task Force, I spoke with hundreds of business owners each week. This feedback and open dialogue shaped my advocacy to our provincial and federal partners and allowed for programs that would better support our small businesses.

The unique and devastating impact on the hospitality industry throughout the pandemic does not need to be re-stated. It's a tough business that relies heavily on face-to-face interactions to stay profitable. As we're once again asking folks to stay home, all levels of government are working together to support the hospitality sector through another lockdown.

The feedback from business owners will be especially critical as we look towards our long-term recovery. Thank you to everyone who has and continues to share their thoughts on how we can move forward. Our incredible small businesses and hospitality sector are a strength of Toronto, and we're looking forward to growing back even stronger. #inthistogether

CGBEU-yhwye.caption:
#CycleForMichael
Last year, Michael Pirovolakis was diagnosed with a rare neurodegenerative disease called SPG50. This disease will take away Michael's ability to use his limbs and limit his mental capacity.

In an effort to raise funds and awareness to fight this terrible disease, Michael's father Terry has set off on a solo bicycle journey from Toronto to Ottawa. Terry is brand new to cycling, and with more than 400 kms of riding, thousands of meters of climbing, and windswept open roads, this is a very challenging endeavor. 

A few weeks ago, I completed the ride from Toronto to Ottawa with @toronto_hustle to support their efforts. Terry and I have exchanged messages about routes, equipment, and fueling strategies. He’ll be arriving in Ottawa shortly, after four days of riding, and I'm very proud of him.
 
I can tell you that Michael's parents', Terry and Georgia, are relentless - their spirit of love, hope, and determination embodies the best of humanity - nothing will stop them in their quest to @cure_spg50. If you're in a position to donate, please consider giving, or share their story and help spread the word. Link in bio.

CGA2WRCBCu6.caption:
Surface transit has played an incredibly important role throughout the pandemic. Our buses and streetcars have moved thousands of essential workers across the city every day, keeping it functioning over the past several months. More folks are heading to work and traffic volumes have increased and we need to continue making sure the riders on surface transit can still move safely and efficiently.

Priority bus routes will result in more frequent service and less crowding as well as more efficient commutes for all users. This is a huge step towards supporting the Toronto suburbs that have been historically underserved by transit but heavily rely on it to get around. More info on the project at the link in my bio! #TTC #Transit

CF7XVQoBRjl.caption:
With fall upon us and back to school well underway, a lot of us are thinking about safety in the community. This has been a tough year for all of us not just with the pandemic but also the difficult but important conversations we have been having as a community around racism experienced by Black, Indigenous and People of Colour (BIPOC) residents.
With these conversations and the experience of our most vulnerable neighbours top of mind, I would like to invite you to a community safety town hall with me and Superintendent Reuben Stroble from Toronto Police Services, 55 Division. The meeting will be held virtually on Wednesday, October 7th from 6:30 pm to 8:30 pm. Register at the link in my bio to receive the virtual meeting details!

CFkQDNbhziB.caption:

CFKSg2vh83h.caption:
The City just released it's COVID-19 Housing and Homeless Recovery Plan to fast-track 3,000 permanent, affordable homes in 24 months.

Intergovernmental partnerships are critical to relieving pressure on our housing and shelter system. CDRZ-o1hy9j.caption:
The situation facing us and all municipalities, underscores the precarious financial nature of cities. This branch of government is closest to people and does the heavy lifting, delivering critical services that folks rely on in their day-to-day lives.

And yet, despite the extensive breadth and scope of services we’re expected to deliver, we are the least equipped with the financial tools and mechanisms to pay for them. Years of successive downloading, shrugging off responsibility and putting it on the back of property taxes and user fees, means we are particularly vulnerable to these sort of shocks and stresses. I'll continue to push and advocate for a New Deal for Cities.

More exciting news for the East End today: we're welcoming two Housing Now Phase 2 sites to our neighbourhood. These are city-owned properties where we'll partner to build around 150 affordable homes for families in our community, on a fast-track timeline. These sites will not only bring much needed housing relief but also investment to the East End.

The two sites include: part of the proposed Danforth Garage/Coxwell Barns redevelopment at Coxwell and Danforth, and the Harvey's site at 1631 Queen Street East. In total, we're anticipating around 150 affordable new units across these sites. Housing Now Phase 2 should deliver up to 1,700 new affordable units city-wide. Phase 1 which is in progress is delivering over 10,000 new homes, of which an estimated 3,900 are affordable. #HousingNow

CAnYk0RBhQS.caption:
Mayor @JohnTory just announced the City’s plan to fast-track implementing 40km of cycling infrastructure across Toronto, including the Danforth! This summer you’ll be able to ride Danforth in a protected lane, enjoy a safer and more attractive pedestrian environment, and take advantage of more patio space. 
The road to economic recovery goes through our main streets. Over the course of the pandemic I’ve talked to hundreds of businesses and we know that bringing people back to places like the Danforth will be critical. This is about making Danforth your destination, for now and into the future. 
The pilot would see an unprecedented $4 million investment to enhance our public realm, create new opportunities for patios, provide dedicated parking, and add the infrastructure we need so that people can walk, ride and roll through our neighbourhood.

This is the transformative change that Toronto needs. Believe in the East End, and I’ll see you on Danforth!

CADmpHhFMCP.caption:
“It’s heartbreaking that programs are being rolled out in six weeks, because businesses don’t have six weeks. How many are we going to lose between now and mid-May?” Thoughtful piece from @nowtoronto (link in bio!) on how we can help small businesses both throughout the pandemic as well as in a post-COVID world.

Here are four ways we could save small businesses right now:
1) Tenant-centres rent relief
2) Moratorium on commercial evictions
3) Tax policy reform
4) Vacant storefront tax

More support is needed to ensure we have local favourites to return to after the pandemic.

B7J7syAFkTj.caption:
The City budget for 2020 was released today. At the dawn of a new decade, we’ll be focusing on making improvements to how you live, work and get around in our City. With the investment into the City Building Fund, we’ll make significant improvements to transit and housing #topoli
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
$13.2 billion will be invested into Transit - nearly doubling our prior investment into state-of-good-repair. An additional $5.3 billion will be invested into affordable housing initiatives in accordance with the HousingTO 10-year plan.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
$67 million will be invested into poverty reduction, climate change, safety/security, and transit. We’ll be hiring 62 new paramedics, over 300 police officers, and 121 TTC operators. We’ll be preserving all City services while implementing $891 million in efficiencies. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
This isn’t the end of the budgeting process. I’ll be hosting an East York budget consultation next Wednesday, January 15th, from 7 - 9pm. Residents always come first - that's why we want to hear your thoughts and opinions on the budget so we can better understand your priorities.

B6OqTISF622.caption: Today was a special day. I welcomed community members from the ODSP Action Coalition to share their personal stories on the challenges of living with a disability. It was harrowing. No one should be losing sleep because their housing isn't secure or their social programs are losing funding. If the Province continues on this path of changing the definition of disability, 120,000 Torontonians could lose $400 a month. It's inhumane to put even further pressure on a demographic that is already struggling. A massive thank you to Claude and Danielle for their bravery and honesty in sharing their stories. Thankfully, my council colleagues recognized the importance of this issue and their votes showed it. We received unanimous support on the motion to protect the definition of disability.

BxkcfFjhkjZ.caption:
If we’re building new homes, they should be affordable and come with critical infrastructure like transit, parks, childcare, and recreation facilities. This week in Council I spoke about the Provincial Government's proposed Bill 108 and the consequences it will have for Toronto. 
The province's approach isn’t just cavalier - it’s contradictory. On one hand we are being told that we must build more housing to improve affordability without any tools to actually fund, build, or secure affordable homes. On the other hand, we are choking the mechanisms we have to build the infrastructure we need to support new growth. 
Let me be clear, I think growth should pay for growth and Bill 108 will have consequences for the people of Toronto.

Buried in the technicalities are very real impacts putting community projects at risk including:
- 21 Toronto Public Library expansion and renovation projects
- 106 new or expanded parks
- 17 community recreation centres
- 5 pools
- 4 arenas
- Over 200 playground improvement projects
- 12 child-care centres with some 583 spaces

BnkTXWbhwwO.caption:
#CantStopWontStop - Today, the Province signaled its intention to use the ‘notwithstanding clause’ to override the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. Using the notwithstanding clause should be reserved for legislative issues of national or provincial significance – it should be a very high bar – and it should be for exceptional circumstances. I’m not sure why the City of Toronto’s ward boundaries have been deemed so pressing that this sort of drastic action is necessary. It shouldn’t be used for a pet project. 
It’s unfortunate that these types of rash decisions from the Province take our attention away from the issues that matter most to residents – affordable housing, building the downtown relief line, improving road safety, and supporting our local businesses. I will always stand up for our community – I will always fight for Toronto – but the noise from the Province won’t distract me from working on the hopes and concerns of Beaches-East York residents. 
Since Bill 5 passed, I’ve made my view on the matter clear – I think the Province’s timing was terrible, and I believe we’re better off with more representation than less.  But with the Province moving to reduce Toronto City Council to 25-wards, I committed to being a champion for all of Beaches – East York. The chaos today didn’t change that. I’m going to continue knocking doors across BEY. 
We will know more in the coming days, but whether ends being 25 or 47 wards, my name will be on the ballot. I ‘m running to make a positive difference in our community, whatever shape that may ultimately take.

BiPDrjvBTFa.caption:
City building is really about community building. One of our recent @civicactiongtha sessions explored the importance of giving voice and platform to those with lived-experience, and the value of user-centred approaches. 
We need to be honest and upfront about the challenges facing different communities, and then have a conversation about equity, access, and resources. Start by building meaningful relationships - go to where the people are - and reflect on how you can help. The community usually has the answer - and sometimes the best thing you can do, is open the door, and get out of the way. #DiverseCityFellows

BhFvFhrA0go.caption:
Last week, the City of Toronto announced @gregglintern_rpp appointment as Chief Planner and Executive Director of @cityplanto. I’ve had the chance to work with Gregg in the Chief Planner’s Office over the past few months, and I’ve come to know him as a visionary practitioner, but equally important, a deeply kind and thoughtful leader. 
Today, #Toronto faces a tension between enjoying the benefits of growth, while being challenged by the equity of these investments. As the City continues to grow, many residents are feeling the squeeze on the subway and the escalating costs of housing. Toronto’s challenges are extensive and complex. 
For months, Gregg has been talking about the importance of investment across the City, and delivering transit, complete communities, and new opportunity to the #416suburbs. It’s about brining an equity lens to strategic investments, and ensuring we focus on community building – not just development. It’s a long road ahead, but Toronto will benefit from this kind of thinking. 
Tomorrow, the Ontario Municipal Board (OMB), the quasi-judicial body that deals with development proposal appeals, will become the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal (LPAT). OMB reform may be one of the most influential changes to Ontario’s planning profession. It’s about greater municipal responsibility and accountability in decision-making. It’s about delivering a policy-led planning regime. Our new Chief Planner brings more than 30 years of experience working on many of Toronto’s most influential planning projects – in a time of legislative reform – this will be invaluable.

BgkYtiqlxii.caption:
Final consultation meeting for the Danforth Avenue Planning Study was well-attended. Feedback over the past twelve months indicates this is a community that celebrates diversity and vibrancy, and wants to ensure that #Danforth continues to evolve as a liveable, walkable destination. 
The growth coming to Danforth will consist of both residential and employment opportunities, and generally occur in a mid-rise, mixed-use form. Importantly, this growth must be balanced with green spaces, investments in community services and facilities, and come with an emphasis on complete streets.

Thanks to @cityplanto for all of their professional work, to date. While change can be challenging, I think the policy directions are balanced, pragmatic, and reflect the feedback from the community.

BgBtbHrnXby.caption: We spent the weekend in King City at an intensive retreat exploring ideas around leadership, overcoming challenges, and resilience. I'm continually impressed by the talent, strength, and creativity of the @civicactiongtha DiverseCity Fellows group - but as we shared more time together, I was struck by their compassion, self-awareness, and humility. On the surface, it's easy to take for granted the composure and professionalism we try to deliver in our day to day work - but it's important to remember, even the most collected individuals have experienced trauma, setbacks and defeat. We all have moments of vulnerability. How we respond to change and adversity helps to define us and build our strength going forward. We don't typically get to have these types of conversations with friends and colleagues - but I found the process of self-reflection to be valuable, leaving me with renewed optimism and energy.

Criteriums are the coliseums for modern day gladiators. The format is raw and exposed – you can feel the nerves and tension as the riders stage on the startline. With nearly 200 cyclists packed against the barriers, positioning is critical as riders negotiate a series of technical turns, launch attacks, and sprint for primes. 
For spectators, crits provide a display of courage, speed, technical acumen and horsepower. Riders explore the limits of their physical abilities and take calculated risks.

The configuration and structure plays well in North America, providing great sight lines, opportunities to collaborate with local businesses, and brining fans closer to the action. 
My latest piece with @soigneurs  takes a closer look at the largest race series in North America, @bcsuperweek, and provides an overview of the fourth episode in @toronto_hustle HOLDFAST webseries.

BZTUM_Ngcit.caption:
Racing in the heart of the city helps shape our collective consciousness around 21st century sport, and what cycling means to an active and engaged local community. It exposes the sport to new and curious audiences, and strengthens an important connection with our #neighbourhoods. 
The #Ossington #Criterium takes place in one of Toronto’s most vibrant and eclectic neighbourhoods. Historically, Ossington’s legacy is one of industry – the strip dotted with tire shops, hardware stores and kitchen cabinet outlets. However, more recently, an influx of bars, restaurants and boutiques has transformed the stretch of South Ossington between Queen and Dundas into Toronto’s best three blocks for drinking and dining. The prominent location of the event, and strategic partnership with the local @ossingtonbia brought thousands of fans out to the course, pressed against the barriers lining the main street. 
Cycling in North America needs more of this – curated events that provide something for families, local businesses and racers – while reflecting the growing diversity of our sport.

I sat down with @soigneurs to discuss the state of cycling, and provide a bit more insight into HOLDFAST Episode 3:

Grateful for the opportunity to join @friendsofsimonwiesenthal’s Yom HaShoah Commemoration at City Hall today. On Holocaust Memorial Day and all days, we remember the six million Jews who perished during the Holocaust and those who fought back and survived. In Toronto and beyond, we remember the bravery of the survivors and reflect on the lives that have been lost to antisemitism and hatred.

Today's remarks from Eva Meisels, a Holocaust survivor, and the FSWC's Legacy Portrait Project serve as an all too important reminder of the tragedy of the Holocaust, and the importance of continuing the fight against antisemitism.

CjIhYokA3g5.caption:
Today is National Day of #TruthAndReconciliation. An important day for all of us here in Canada to remember, learn, and reflect about the survivors, children, families, and communities who have been impacted by the Residential School System. Yesterday, I had the opportunity to join Indigenous community leaders from across Toronto in a Sunrise Ceremony to honour those affected and to recommit to action, and truth and reconciliation efforts.

This year, the City adopted the Reconciliation Action Plan 2022-2023 to advance truth, justice, and reconciliation, and it builds on the City's existing commitments to Indigenous Peoples through 28 meaningful actions. There is no doubt we have a long way to go, but I will always stay committed to our ongoing efforts. #EveryChildMatters #revillagizing 

.
.
.
.

Chdje9UtRrM.caption:
I’m left with a profound sense of both gratitude and heartbreak hearing the stories from families who suffered losses due to the Dieppe raid in WW2. 

I was joined by East Yorkers in Dieppe Park this evening (which was named by the East York Council at the time due to the involvement of so many East Yorkers in the raid ) and together, we commemorated the 80th anniversary of that fateful day. 

East Yorkers joined in to share their family history, and speak of those who made the ultimate sacrifice. We must continue passing on their legacy and never forget what they gave up for our Country, and city. #LestWeForget

.
.
.
.
.

CgfLOXVpmXi.caption:
Our office has been notified that an individual was knocking on doors in the O’Connor Drive area, identifying himself as a City of Toronto Contractor connected to an upcoming Basement Flooding Protection Program project and asking permission to enter private homes. This individual is not affiliated with the City of Toronto or our Contractors.

Access to your home is not required for this work at this time as the project is still in tender and a contractor has not yet been assigned. Once a contractor is selected, a pre-construction notice identifying the contractor will be shared along with a number to schedule an appointment for an inspection at a later date. The contractor will not show up asking for entry without prior notice and all inspection staff will wear photo I.D. clearly identifying that they are employed by the contractor.

Should you be approached by someone asking to enter your home:
•  Do not let the person in your home
•  Call TPS Division 55 at tel:4168082222 to report the activity
•  Call 311 to report the activity

Please share this information with your neighbours, and reach out if you have any further questions or require further information.
.
.
.
.
.
.

CgcVBDXADU5.caption:
Part of protecting the most vulnerable in our City means protecting current renters and folks in precarious housing positions. As the cost of housing continues to climb, we need to keep doing the work to stop us from losing the stock of rental units that are actually affordable and within financial reach, while adding more opportunities. That means protecting against renovictions, creating more rental units, and looking at ways to address our City’s low 1% rental vacancy.

The recommendations from our Housing Secretariat are an important piece to address the large scale problem of #TO's housing crisis. We must keep raising the voices of residents, working with our government partners, and finding new solutions for those who need it most in our City. We can keep making housing happen, and these recommendations are a positive path forward.

.
.
.
.

CgWrh5XAf70.caption:
Four years ago, Reese Fallon's life was tragically cut short during the 2018 Danforth Shooting. Reese was an optimist and an advocate for change, two qualities that reflect the best of #BEY. It was a profound honour to join with the family, friends, and loved ones of all the victims of this devastating event, and remember the deep impacts they made throughout their lives here in the East End.

Reese’s legacy deserves to be forever memorialized. After months of work with the community, I'm pleased our City will be moving ahead on an official laneway renaming in her namesake in the coming months. It's a small way we can honour the outsized presence she had in the lives of many. 

#DanforthStrong

.
.
.

Around 500 agenda items later ... and that's a wrap! We have officially finished our Council term, with so much progress made a long the way. This level of government has worked hard to deliver more affordable housing, #ClimateChange action, safer streets, #SmallBusiness supports - and much more. I'm proud of the work we have done through the last 4 days, and past 4 years, but it couldn't have been accomplished without each and every one of you.

Together, we've moved ahead to deliver community-led change and bring the voices of #BEY into the Council chambers. It's been an honour to represent your ideas, feedback, and suggestions here at City Hall. Thanks for all of your hard work and contributions this term. Our community - and our city - is all the stronger for it. #BelieveInTheEast

Our Muslim friends in the #BeachesEastYork community and around the country begin celebrating Eid al-Adha today. With one of the largest #Eid gatherings in Canada, our team was humbled to attend Eid prayers at Dentonia Park this morning.

Celebrations are underway for those in our community marking the end of the annual religious pilgrimage to Mecca, called Hajj, including getting together for traditional prayers, sharing a special meal with loved ones, providing charity and support to those in need, and partaking in gift-giving. This three-to-four-day-long celebration is a time spent reflecting on life lessons of generosity, community, and service.

I would also like to take this opportunity to acknowledge and appreciate the continuous contributions of our Muslim neighbours in shaping our much loved Beaches-East York community. May the spirit of compassion, generosity and community continue throughout the year. To all those observing and celebrating at #Dentonia or elsewhere this weekend, I wish you and your loved ones a wonderful celebration.

#EidMubarak!

Cfj5X-fJU9H.caption:
It’s been an incredible weekend celebrating #CanadaDay with so many across #BEY.

After two years apart, our #EastEnd energy was truly back in full force. From the return of the historic @eastyorkcanday parade, to festivities at our 4 Legions (including numerous trips into the dunk tank), 2 official fireworks shows, celebrations at Stan Wadlow, and Shomoy Mela back at Dentonia Park - our community was out making #BEY a warm and welcoming place to celebrate the best of being Canadian.

As we celebrated with gratitude, we’re reminded that Canada Day is more than just an opportunity to cheer for our country. It’s also an important day of reflection.

While we embrace how far we have come, we must also look in to our past, acknowledge the pain and oppression of Indigenous peoples on which our country is built on, and channel that reflection into continued action on Truth & Reconciliation.

As a land of opportunity and refuge for many, we are incredibly lucky to live in the greatest country on earth. And that greatness exists because of the different cultures and unique backgrounds that make Canada diverse, and our commitment to building a bright future together.

As we celebrate how far we’ve come, let’s recognize the sacrifice of those that have made it possible, and keep creating the  opportunities, reflections, and collaborations for a better future for all that call Canada and Toronto home. 🇨🇦🍁

.
.
.
.
.

CfE-lNxJfy_.caption:
"The difficult but vital work of community-led change and collaboration is how we’ll get the best outcomes for Toronto’s housing future, together."

It cannot be overstated: to meaningfully address the #housing crisis, we must shift our approach on the measures that will provide better housing options for our current and future neighbours.

For too long the forces of intertia and status quo have played an outsized role in the housing available in our city, and we've reached the breaking point. If we want Toronto to remain a place of opportunity and prosperity for all, it's essential that the we step up to meet this generational challenge. It'll take a series of thoughtful, practical, and innovative measures - and fostering conversations across our communities on the kind of city we need to build together.

Read my full op-ed in @ontarioplanners Y magazine ⬆️

Cszj-OQtdG9.caption:
Today, I announced my plan to expand library hours and make sure every branch is open seven days a week.

Our public libraries are beloved places.

They are where we meet and learn. They provide programs for people of all ages, whether you’re a senior with a book club, a student who needs some quiet space to read, or a new parent with a toddler who wants to hear stories.

Right now, only 19 Toronto Public Library branches are open year-round on Sundays and 30 are closed on Mondays.

My plan will ensure all 100 public libraries are open seven days a week, and have expanded weekday hours of libraries across the city.

I’m thrilled to have been joined by @brandon_4948 & @local4948 and to have their support.

Our libraries couldn’t exist without the library workers who help us find the information we’re looking for, run programs, and make our libraries the community hubs we know and love.

My mother was a survivor, with an innate sense of justice.

She persisted through the Japanese invasion, domestic violence, immigrating to Canada, and so much more. She came into her political identity based on life experience.

She personified strength, and community care.
No one left our home without a meal.

If there’s one lesson that she taught me and Jack, it was that we’re here on earth to make sure those who don’t have enough, can survive.

What a wonderful day to celebrate women who mother, who care, and persist.

Happy Mother’s Day!

There are thousands of people without a roof over their heads in our city, and even more are just a few paycheques away from losing their home.

The wealthiest in our city can chip in a bit more on the sale of luxury homes so we can house 1000s of people.

I will create 1,000 new rent supplements to help people secure permanent housing, and ask the provincial and federal gov'ts to match our investment to create 2,000 more.

I will create new 24/7 respite spaces, where people can access a shower, meals, a bed, and critical services.

I will create a fund to provide things like wrap-around support services, drop-in programming, and additional shelter options. I’ll let the community lead by working with community agencies, front-line workers and people with lived experience to determine how best to use it.

By introducing a luxury homes tax on homes sold for over $3M we’ll raise millions for those who need it most. 

We’ll be able to provide housing and support for thousands of people. Homelessness is an emergency and we need this funding in place today.

The City’s approach of pushing unhoused people around from parks to transit, to libraries, and back has been shameful. Unhoused people deserve dignity.

We can create a more affordable, safe, and caring Toronto.

Fairness is at the heart of this.

We are in this together.

Families are forced to spend a huge chunk of their income on rent, and young people are moving out of the  entirely.

As part of my City Homes Plan, the City will act as a public developer to build 25,000 rent-controlled homes over 8 years on land that we already own.

Our housing crisis is urgent—we can’t count on private developers alone to offer people an affordable place to live. 

We have to take control. Using the tools and land we have available to us today to build the homes people need now.

CryXD1ULOhA.caption:

With a decade-long gap between the closing of the RT and opening of the subway, Scarborough transit riders are being stranded. 

Today I'm announcing my plan to keep transit riders moving. 

My plan will take buses off the street and onto a dedicated busway from Kennedy Station to Scarborough Town Centre, using the existing RT corridor and new bus-only lanes.

This will save Scarborough transit riders 20 minutes on their commute—valuable time to spend with friends and family.

Poor planning and political inaction is leaving Scarborough behind. I'm not going to wait for the province to fund this: it will be funded by the money saved by transitioning the eastern Gardiner into a ground-level boulevard.

It's time Scarborough was treated fairly.

Learn more: oliviachow.ca/scarborough_busway
